definition: A positively charged particle in the nucleus of an atom, with relative mass 1 and relative charge $+1$.
An uncharged particle in the nucleus of an atom, with relative mass 1; isotopes of an element differ in their number of neutrons.
A negatively charged particle, relative charge $-1$, that occupies the space outside the nucleus; its mass is negligible compared with a proton's.
The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom, symbol $Z$; it decides which element the atom belongs to.
Atoms of the same element, with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons; they have the same chemical properties but different physical properties.
An atom or group of atoms with an overall charge, because it has gained or lost electrons.
The weighted mean mass of the atoms of an element, relative to one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, symbol $A_\text{r}$; it has no units.
A graph of relative abundance against mass-to-charge ratio, $m/z$; for an element, each single-atom peak is an isotope and its height shows how common that isotope is.
